title: Import a Large SQL File in MAMP / MAMP PRO
description: MAMP bundles its own PHP and MySQL with their own limits. Here's how to import a big database without the phpMyAdmin upload error.
author: SQLSplit

content.text: MAMP runs its own isolated PHP and MySQL stack. That's why editing your system php.ini does nothing — MAMP ignores it. You have to edit MAMP's copy, or go around phpMyAdmin entirely.

Stop and restart the servers from the MAMP window. In MAMP PRO you can edit php.ini directly under File → Edit Template → PHP.
Import from the command line instead
MAMP's mysql client is the most reliable route for big files. The socket and binary live inside the MAMP folder:
The default MAMP MySQL user is root with password root. The --socket flag matters — MAMP's MySQL listens on its own socket, not the system default, so plain `mysql` from Homebrew won't connect to it.

content.title: ERROR 2002 (HY000): Can't connect to local MySQL server
content.text: You're hitting the system MySQL socket instead of MAMP's. Always pass --socket=/Applications/MAMP/tmp/mysql/mysql.sock, or add --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8889 to use MAMP's TCP port.
Or split and import in chunks
Don't want to touch config files or the terminal? Split the dump below MAMP's upload cap and feed the chunks through phpMyAdmin one at a time.

faq.question: Why doesn't editing php.ini change MAMP's upload limit?
faq.answer: MAMP uses its own bundled PHP with a php.ini inside /Applications/MAMP/bin/php/php{VERSION}/conf/. Editing the macOS system php.ini has no effect. Edit MAMP's copy for the version selected in preferences, then restart the servers.

faq.question: What is the default MAMP MySQL username and password?
faq.answer: Both username and password are 'root'. MySQL runs on port 8889 by default and uses the socket at /Applications/MAMP/tmp/mysql/mysql.sock.

faq.question: How do I connect to MAMP MySQL from the terminal?
faq.answer: Use MAMP's own client at /Applications/MAMP/Library/bin/mysql and pass --socket=/Applications/MAMP/tmp/mysql/mysql.sock, or connect over TCP with --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8889.
